changelog: - **Vertical capability gate on the shell and sidebar** (#2351, epic #2348). A tenant's `Organization.vertical` now decides which modules its shell shows: `src/lib/verticals.ts` already declares each vertical's capability set, and this wires it into the navigation. Capability-tagged nav links (`NavLink.capability`) survive only for an org whose vertical carries that capability — the mentorship, placement and sourcing admin links (`/admin/mentors`, `/admin/mentorship`, `/admin/mentor-applications`, `/admin/mentee-activity`, `/admin/offers`, `/admin/requisitions`, `/admin/interview-requests`, `/interviews`, `/admin/sources`) fall away for a vertical that lacks the module, while every untagged link is always shown. `visibleNavLinks()` does the filtering (pure, unit-tested); the three nav components and the command palette take the resolved capability set as a prop, resolved server-side per request by `shellCapabilities(orgId)` in the layout. The `/mentor` and `/portal` shells additionally redirect a vertical that has switched the mentorship module off entirely. INTERNSHIP carries every capability, so all of this is a strict no-op for today's product — the same sidebar, the same shells, proven by an INTERNSHIP e2e that asserts nothing is hidden. The write-path gate (a hidden module must also refuse a direct POST) is the next slice, #2352.
